civilopediaText.text: The five layers of power

1. Rank. Base strength: Rank One 8, Rank Two 14, Rank Three 22, Rank Four 32, Rank Five 44, Rank Six 60, Rank Seven 85, Rank Eight 115, the Venerable 280. Clan Masters of a rank have the same strength.

2. Path attainment (comprehension). Four tiers stack: Master +10% at any rank, Grandmaster +15% from rank three, Great Grandmaster +20% from rank six, Supreme Grandmaster +25% from rank eight: +70% at the top. Each tier opens a new kind of power: the Master the path's hit on every attack it makes, the Grandmaster a second effect and the mortal killer move, the Great Grandmaster a domain or a new art and the immortal killer move, the Supreme Grandmaster the path's peak.

3. Dao marks, the quantity of dao. Tiers I to V give +5%, +10%, +15%, +20% and +10 HP healing, +30% and +15 HP healing. Every tier also raises the path's hit: extra damage 4/5/6/8/10/12, status turns 2/2/2/3/3/4, healing 5/6/8/10/12/15, XP 2/3/4/5/6/8, stolen stones 10/15/20/25/30/40%, movement 1/1/1/1/2/2 (no marks, then I to V; a path may multiply them). The Master's promotion lists what each tier adds.

Dao marks grow one tier every 20 turns on Standard for a path Master of rank three or more; an immortal also gains one for every immortal it kills and every heavenly tribulation it survives. Mortals stop at tier II. Rank seven needs tier II, rank eight tier III, the Venerable tier IV.
4. Gu. Each path's Gu comes with its Master. Every immortal Gu of your own path that your clan owns adds 5% strength; one of a strongly clashing path takes 5% away.
5. Conflicts. A second path whose dao marks clash with the first costs 5% to 25% strength.
Killer moves

A unit-action button, so only you use them: for one turn the path family's burst plus the path's hit at full power (twice that for the immortal move). The mortal move costs 15 stones, the immortal move 5 green grape essence.
Example

A Rank Six fire-path Great Grandmaster with Dao Marks III: strength 60, +45% from attainment and +15% from dao marks. Each attack inflicts Burning for 3 turns; each attack deals 6 extra damage; domain: enemies beside it fight 10% weaker.
How long an immortal lives

A clan's Lifespan Gu are its immortals' lifespan. Reaching each rank adds to the stock and a higher rank burns it more slowly, so every rank climbed makes an immortal live longer. Numbers on Standard speed; the other speeds scale the turns.
Rank six: +20 Lifespan Gu on ascending; burns one every 10 turns, so its own gift lasts about 200 turns.
Rank seven: +25 Lifespan Gu on advancing; burns one every 15 turns, so its own gift lasts about 375 turns.
Rank eight: +35 Lifespan Gu on advancing; burns one every 20 turns, so its own gift lasts about 700 turns.
The Venerable: +60 Lifespan Gu on becoming a Venerable; burns one every 30 turns, so its own gift lasts about 1800 turns.
All the clan's immortals share one stock, each burning at its own rank's rate. With none left an immortal wastes away (7 damage a turn) and heals only by pillaging; one Lifespan Gu ends that at once.
How to add lifespan
1. Climb. Every rank reached adds Lifespan Gu (above): the surest way.
2. Green land. From Calamity Lore, every 8 owned forest, jungle or marsh tiles of each kind give one with a 15% chance each turn: keep your woods and swamps, settle near them.

3. Immortal Gu and inheritances: Year Gu gives 1 every 3 turns; Years Flow Like Water gives 2 every 5 turns for 10 green grape essence while the clan holds more than 9; Red Lotus Inheritance gives 1 every 5 turns.
4. The market. Treasure Yellow Heaven sells 3 Lifespan Gu for 120 stones.
5. Conquest. A captured city keeps its immortal Gu and inheritances, so the ones above can be seized.
What takes lifespan
Wisdom Gu: takes 1 every 5 turns.
While a Venerable lives, every clan loses one each 10 turns.
The Zombie Alliance's immortals never age (it gains one per immortal each 10 turns) but make no essence.
Immortals against mortal clans

An immortal outclasses any mortal army: strength 60, 85 and 115 at ranks six to eight against 44 at rank five, before its path, and it crosses the region walls. That is the reward for a long, hard climb: ascension needs a rank-five Master, the three qi and luck, and every rank above needs a survived tribulation, dao marks and essence.

name: Gu World: Gu Hunger and Food

civilopediaText.text: Every Gu eats

A Gu that eats a Gu food (moon orchid, wild boar, jade or wine) takes it from the clan's stock every turn. When the clan is short, every Gu eating that food is weakened at once and its hunger meter rises each turn: a status on the unit shows the percent. At 100% the Gu rolls its chance to die, then the meter starts again. Feed the clan and the meter clears.

Hunger rate by rank: rank 1 +33% a turn (50% death chance at 100%), rank 2 +20% a turn (50% death chance at 100%), rank 3 +14% a turn (50% death chance at 100%), rank 4 +11% a turn (50% death chance at 100%). The lower the rank, the faster the hunger.
Where the food comes from: moon orchid and wild boar from their improved tiles and the Gu Feeding House, jade from mined jade, wine only from the Tavern.
Other Gu eat primeval stones: each raises its unit's upkeep, usually by 10%. When the clan's stones fall below zero, every unit fights 20% weaker.

What a path's hit leaves on its target. A status ticks at the start of the target's own turn.
Poisoned: Venom works through the body: damage at every turn start until it fades.
Charmed: Charm saps the will: weaker attacks while it lasts.
Sealed: A restriction seal cuts the unit off from healing; only pillage restores it.
Phantom Veil: After a heavy blow the body turns insubstantial for a moment: much harder to hit.
Shaken: A mind-path move has shaken the unit's resolve: weaker in battle.
Burning: Fire-path flames cling to the body: 8 damage at every turn start until they die out.
Frozen: Ice-path frost locks the limbs: 1 movement less and 15% weaker attacks.
Bleeding: Open wounds from bone, blade or blood: 6 damage at every turn start.
Blinded: Light or cloud fills the eyes: 2 sight less and 10% weaker.
Soul-Torn: The soul is wounded: 15% weaker, and half the battle experience.
Dazed: Sound, dream or ink has muddled the mind: 1 movement less and 10% weaker.
Guard Broken: The guard is broken, by force, metal, venom or a weakness exposed: 20% weaker when defending.
Entangled: Roots or a formation hold the legs: 2 movement less.
Shocked: Lightning runs through the body: 25% weaker.
Doomed: Fortune has turned, or heaven itself frowns: 10% weaker and 5 damage at every turn start.
Aged: Time-path years pour into the body: 10% weaker when defending and 5 damage at every turn start.
Weighted: Earth or starlight presses down: 1 movement less and 15% weaker when defending.
